🇲🇽🎙️ <u>SHEINBAUM TO THE CENSORSHIP CHORUS: "THERE'S NEVER BEEN MORE FREEDOM"</u>

The same media owners who once took phone calls from Los Pinos — "fire this host, he's talking bad about me" — now scream censorship over audience-rights guidelines that are still in public consultation and were agreed with the broadcasters' own chamber. Sheinbaum's answer: "There's a TV network that spends 24 hours trashing the government. When have we ever asked for a host to be removed? There will be no censorship — it's our conviction."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>WORLD CUP'S DARK STAT: DOMESTIC VIOLENCE REPORTS IN MEXICO UP 50%</u>

While Mexico hosted the World Cup, the Red Nacional de Refugios registered a 50% jump in domestic violence complaints during the tournament's first weeks — calls, WhatsApp messages, pleas for help. It's not the football, specialists say; it's the machismo that was already there. Endireh's baseline: 70.1% of Mexican women have experienced gender violence. The party exposed the wound. Naming it is the first step to healing it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ANOTHER MEXICAN DIES IN ICE CUSTODY — PRICILIANO TREJO, 29, HAD LEUKEMIA</u>

Priciliano Trejo asked ICE for medical attention on July 6. He had leukemia. He died in a Georgia hospital after weeks inside Stewart Detention Center — one of the largest immigration jails in the US. He was 29. Mexico has filed criminal complaints over 17 Mexicans dead in US custody since Trump returned; Trejo makes 18. A sick man begged for a doctor and got a cell.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>ZHENLI YE GON GETS 15 YEARS — MEXICO CLOSES A TWO-DECADE CASE</u>

Nineteen years after Mexico seized $205 million in cash from his Lomas de Chapultepec mansion — the largest cash bust in the country's history — a federal judge sentenced Zhenli Ye Gon to 15 years and a day for laundering $33 million to tax havens. No sentence substitutes, no conditional release, political rights suspended. The case Washington once used to lecture Mexico about impunity just ended with a Mexican court, Mexican evidence and a conviction.

🇲🇽📈 <u>FISCAL DISCIPLINE PAYS: MEXICO'S DEBT AT 51% OF GDP — 1.6 POINTS BELOW TARGET</u>

Mexico's public debt closed June at 51% of GDP, 1.6 percentage points below what was programmed, with the budget deficit 358 billion pesos under target and a primary surplus of 115 billion in the first semester, Hacienda reported. VAT collection grew 10.6% in real terms — the best first half since 2014 — while social spending hit record pace: health up 18.3%, education 13.5%, social development up 9.7%, its highest rate for a first semester on record.

The debt sits mostly in pesos, at fixed rates and long maturities, and Fitch, S&P and R&I just reaffirmed Mexico's investment grade. Tax fairly, spend on people, keep the books in order.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>"NO HUMAN IS ILLEGAL": CDMX'S BRUGADA CALLS OUT US ANTI-MIGRANT POLICIES BEFORE 12 CITIES</u>

Hosting mayors and officials from 12 cities across the Americas, Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada didn't mince words: "From Mexico City we energetically condemn the policies that criminalize human mobility." She announced a new Multiservice Center giving migrants legal aid, medical care, housing and social support in one place — on top of doubled shelter capacity and humanitarian brigades that attended thousands this semester.

Bogotá mayor Carlos Fernando Galán backed her up: "Migration represents an opportunity for the development of cities." While Washington builds walls and ICE body counts, Latin America's cities are building the alternative.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>31% OF HUMAN TRAFFICKING CASES IN MEXICO CITY ARE FORCED LABOR, WATCHDOG WARNS</u>

Nearly a third of the human trafficking cases received by Mexico City's Consejo Ciudadano involve forced labor or services, its fifth annual report reveals. Last year 18 people — including minors and foreigners — were rescued after being forced to work in a scam center selling fraudulent raffles; just this month, authorities freed four young people found chained inside improvised cells in an illegal call center.

Interpol estimates fraud-related reports jumped 54% between 2024 and 2025, with victims identified from 66 countries. The new slavery runs on phone lines and laptops — and Mexico is naming it, tracking it and raiding it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN: FEDS CATCH "R1," ALLEGED MASTERMIND OF MAYOR CARLOS MANZO'S MURDER</u>

Federal forces arrested Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, alias "R1," the alleged intellectual author of the November 2025 assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo during the Festival of the Candles. He led Los Rs, one of the most violent CJNG-linked cells operating in Apatzingán, Uruapan and Morelia, tied to extortion, homicides and drug trafficking.

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said 31 people have now been detained in the case — the result of intelligence work by the CNI, the SSPC and Army Special Forces under President Sheinbaum's Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice. Not a single foreign boot on the ground.

🗳️🇲🇽 <u>FAKE PARTY BUSTED: ELECTORAL COURT CONFIRMS FINE OVER 5,000 PHOTOCOPIED "MEMBERS"</u>

Mexico's electoral court (TEPJF) unanimously confirmed a fine of nearly half a million pesos against "México Tiene Vida," the Nuevo León conservative outfit that tried to register as a national political party using more than 5,000 simulated affiliations — photocopies of voter IDs of supposed members.

The INE caught the fraud during its review, denied the registration, and the Sala Superior just shut the door for good. In Mexico, astroturfed right-wing "citizen movements" don't get to photocopy their way onto the ballot.

🇲🇽🌊 <u>MEXICO GOES ALL-IN ON SARGASSUM: 2 BILLION PESOS, MORE SHIPS, A CIRCULAR ECONOMY</u>

While a record sargassum surge floods the Caribbean — 90,538 tons a day floating offshore, 27 times the historical average and four times last year — Mexico isn't waiting for anyone to save its beaches. The federal government is investing 2 billion pesos to intercept the algae at sea: more Navy sargassum vessels (about 250 million pesos each), 50 km of containment barriers, and 150 scientists working to turn the plague into biogas, biofertilizer and bioplastics at a new circular-economy hub in Puerto Morelos.

"This year more sargassum arrived at the beaches of Quintana Roo, and the scientists have to explain why — and also how to recycle the algae," Sheinbaum said. Climate change made the mess; Mexico is building the response.
